title: Guru Nanak grants Babur conditional sovereignty

blocks.text: Babur pleads that he entrusted himself to Daulat Khan only because he had staked everything on Guru Nanak's name, and he now asks the Guru to preserve his honor. Guru Nanak responds with compassion, accepts the petition, and prepares a symbolic act to show how the boon will be measured out.

He asks for Babur's bag of intoxicant and pours out seven handfuls of bhang, granting a line of rule that will run through seven generations. The gift is real, but it is given as a marked favor rather than as an unconditional right.

Guru Nanak then warns that India has been bestowed for a trifling exchange and can also be taken back. Babur immediately protests that a boon once granted should not later be revoked, setting up the Guru's stern answer on the next page.
